data.title: Amid France’s political 'fragmentation', 'a case needs to be made for participatory democracy’
data.description: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Dr. Andrew Smith, Historian of Modern France and Lecturer in Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London. He argues that Marine Le Pen and the National Rally’s commanding position in early presidential polling should not be regarded as an inevitable far-right victory. They are benefiting from familiarity, unity and laser-focused messaging. More fundamentally, however, Smith sees the polling as a reflection of a French electorate shaped by anger, anxiety, economic insecurity and political fatigue. Rather than describing this landscape simply as one of growing “polarization,” he proposes the more revealing concept of “fragmentation.”

data.title: Lack of 'enforcement of EU laws': Consumer products contain 'illegal levels of restricted chemicals'
data.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Hélène Duguy, Senior Environmental Lawyer at ClientEarth. PFAS pollution is widespread, these highly persistent chemicals have been detected in water and soil, food and consumer products, and even the human body. The risks are increasingly well documented, alternatives now exist for many uses, and there is an extensive regulatory framework that is in place. Duguy argues that the central problem is therefore not simply a lack of scientific knowledge or legislation, but rather weak enforcement, slow regulation and corporate resistance. And so hazardous chemicals remain in circulation even when restrictions exist.

data.title: Yemen: Fact-checking videos claiming to show Houthi rebel attacks

Other viral videos falsely linked to Houthi attacks on a Saudi Aramco refinery were also traced to unrelated fires in Texas and Russia. Vedika Bahl fact-checks in Truth or Fake.

data.title: Benedict Cumberbatch on his Earth-saving eco film: ‘We are in the last grab of the extraction era’
data.description: From Obama’s chef to a big cat obsessive, the actor has gathered experts from Alaska, the Amazon and beyond for a film about how to heal our besieged planet. He talks about naysayers, elephant tusks – and the wonders of venison Benedict Cumberbatch is dreading stepping outside. He’s speaking to me from his air-conditioned hotel room in Soho at the peak of the summer heat. Few doubt that climate breakdown was a major cause of those scorchers, with nature, farming and water supplies all placed under huge strain. By midsummer, according to a report co-authored by the Met Office , there were 2,700 excess deaths in England and Wales due to the searing heat. But for Cumberbatch, in a bittersweet way, the record-breaking temperatures have come at a good time. The actor has been on a tour to promote his new documentary, How to Live on Earth. “The irony is not lost on anyone,” he says. “We’re living in the results of climate breakdown so stepping outside is – literally – a call to action.” Continue reading...

data.title: I know why many east Germans vote AfD. And no, it’s not an inherited longing for dictatorship | Carolin Würfel
data.description: Grievance politics has grown in the east of the country where I was born. But west Germans have hard questions to answer too The fear that a fascist, far-right movement would rise to power again in Germany has been with me since my youth. On 6 September, the far-right, anti-immigrant, pro-Kremlin Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) won a landslide in Saxony-Anhalt, becoming the biggest party in the state parliament, with a shocking 44% of the vote, on a record turnout. If it finds a way to power it will be the first far-right party to govern a German state since the Nazi era. The night before the vote, I sent a message to a friend, who, like myself, has an East German background. Was she as worried, scared even, about the vote as I was, I asked. I’d fallen into a loop for days, scrolling videos, reels, reports, interviews done on the ground. And I knew these AfD voters. They could have been relatives, friends of my parents, old teachers, former schoolmates. Why were they saying such incoherent stuff? Continue reading...

data.title: The pirates arrived with AK-47s. They took us hostage – then the torture began
data.description: Chirag Bahri was working on board a tanker when six men seized it. For almost eight months, he and his colleagues were held captive, an experience that would change his life for ever It was at noon on 8 May 2010 when the pirates came. Chirag Bahri remembers the exact time and date because it marked the start of the seven months and 20 days he was held hostage by a gang of Somali pirates. Bahri was 28 at the time, and working as second engineer on a chemical tanker, Marida Marguerite. It was his 12th journey through the Gulf of Aden in the Indian Ocean. It had been a good job for a young man from landlocked Uttar Pradesh in India, and Bahri was about to be promoted. “But then, piracy,” he says. The ship had been 120 miles off the coast of Oman, partway through a run taking benzene – a raw material used in petrochemicals – from Kandla Port in India to Antwerp in Belgium. The piracy problem in the Indian Ocean was well known; Somalis armed with AK-47s were setting out in fast skiffs and taking ships hostage. Yet commercial vessels, including the Marida Marguerite, remained undefended. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A double entendre in every crevice’: what, beyond near-naked tennis, is Sydney Sweeney’s game?
data.description: With her new, semi-nude advert for sports site Novig, the actor cements her reputation as the anti-woke poster girl. But is it real – or just provocation with a soft porn gaze? Bear with me here, but I’m beginning to suspect Sydney Sweeney is a very fine actor. It’s a skill she has been recognised for in the past, of course, winning nominations for Emmys for Euphoria and The White Lotus, but I mean it in a deeper sense, related to her work in advertising rather than drama – can she do more than play a role? Can she make you feel what she’s feeling? In her “controversial” new ad for the sports prediction site Novig (the scare quotes are because, when you’re begging for controversy this hard, you shouldn’t just be handed it on a plate), she adopts the garb of various sports. Her face, body, aspect, gait and mien are all carefully configured to amp up the erotic overtones to the maximum degree, and yet the feeling that beams out of each image is: “This is really going to piss people off, and I couldn’t be more delighted.” Her expression is so speechful that you cannot help but share in some of her hellion joy. Continue reading...

data.title: The wilting rose emoji: what its rise and fall tells us about gen Alpha
data.description: It was the fastest-growing emoji in 2025 – but if you’re older than 16, it has probably passed you by. Now, just as twentysomethings are catching up, it’s over In the 2025 hit Netflix show Adolescence, DI Luke Bascombe’s 13-year-old son, Adam, has to explain to his father the way his generation use heart emojis. “Red means love, purple: horny, yellow: ‘I’m interested, are you interested?’, pink: ‘I’m interested but not in sex,’ orange: ‘You’re going to be fine,’” he explains. “It all has a meaning. Everything has a meaning.” And those meanings are constantly evolving. Take the skull (), for example, which has come to be used as a reaction for finding something funny – a visual shorthand for the slang phrase: “I’m dead.” Or the wilting rose () which was, according to Google data analysed by the New York Times , the fastest-growing emoji in terms of popularity in 2025 – and was the 93rd most used. That the previously obscure wilting rose is now in the top 100 emojis is thanks to generation Alpha (those born between 2010 and 2024), who use it in place of the broken heart emoji () to signify sadness, or ironically, to suggest mock-heartbreak. Continue reading...

data.title: It’s a superfood but natto as we know it. Japan’s slimy fermented beans are coming your way
data.description: Comprised of smelly soya beans held together by strands of mucus, the ancient dish is appearing in health food shops across the world It is smelly, slimy and contains bacteria – and a sizeable number of Japanese wouldn’t touch it with a pair of barge pole-length chopsticks. But after centuries as a breakfast food for Japanese diners with nerves of steel, natto is emerging as a global superfood to rival kimchi , kombucha and kefir . Its exact origins are unknown. Some believe it was introduced to Japan from China by Buddhist monks during the Yayoi period (300BC-AD300), before becoming a staple among rural communities during the Edo period (1603-1868). data.title: No one could stand in the way of this juggernaut! The biggest shocks from the Emmy awards
data.description: There were plenty of upsets, and one show in particular failed terribly. But the night was rightfully dominated by Matthew Rhys and the genuinely scary, genuinely hilarious Widow’s Bay To tell the story of how Hacks performed at last night’s Emmys, you have to acknowledge both its incredible success and its terrible failure. The first is undeniable. Last night, Jean Smart won lead actress in a comedy series yet again. This meant that every time Hacks brought out a new season, Smart won the same award for it. This makes her the first woman to ever win an Emmy for every season of a programme’s run. It’s a history-making achievement, and thoroughly well earned. The flipside of that, however, is that this is all Hacks won last night. One Emmy is better than many shows can even hope to dream of, but the reality is that Hacks swaggered into the Emmys with a record 24 nominations – the most ever for a comedy in a single year – and had the momentum of a huge farewell narrative behind it. But it only ended up winning one for Jean Smart and a Creative Arts Emmy for picture editing. In other words, last night Hacks lost 22 Emmys. Continue reading...

data.title: Fast, furious and potentially fatal: why are supercars suddenly so popular?
data.description: Once the preserve of the ultra-rich, supercars are finding new drivers through rentals, finance deals, influencer culture and the manosphere. But why would anyone want a 200mph vehicle? ‘The £600,000 Lamborghini; that was the first seizure of the operation,” says special chief inspector Geoff Tatman of the Metropolitan police, thinking back to the second weekend of August. “He was stopping at the red lights, revving his engine, waiting for the traffic to clear, then speeding. So on the third time we saw him do it, we stopped him and seized the vehicle.” The car has a top speed of 217mph (350kmh), but the limit on these London streets is 20mph. Over the same weekend, the Metropolitan police seized about 90 more cars with a combined value of more than £8m, an increase on last year’s tally of 72 cars . They were seized for various offences: driving without insurance, driving with incorrect licences or antisocial behaviour. Previously, the Met would have had to let such drivers off with a warning, but the law – section 59 of the Police Reform Act – was strengthened this year to enable the immediate confiscation of vehicles. The seized cars also included a Ferrari Monza worth about £3.4m (the driver only had a provisional UK licence). They were all put on display at Marble Arch, attracting a throng of camera-wielding onlookers (one attender did a seven-hour live blog of the occasion). Many of the supercars apprehended by the Met in August bore Middle Eastern number plates. It has been a growing trend for car owners from the region to spend summer in London, bringing their cars with them (at a cost of £25,000 upwards). The orange Lamborghini that Tatman seized had Dubai plates. Most of the vehicle owners retrieved their cars the next day after paying fines and presenting the correct paperwork. The Lamborghini driver was subsequently seen driving respectfully and not revving his engine. Lessons were learned, although the question remains: why ship a 200mph car to London to drive in a 20mph zone? Continue reading...

data.title: Solo autumn walks for women in the UK and Europe: ‘it should be fun, not daunting’
data.description: Hiking alone in the countryside can be joyous, but for women it can sometimes feel unnerving. Here’s how to enjoy it safely, plus four stunning routes to walk solo I did my first solo hike during a sunny September, seven years ago. After a summer of feeding and ferrying four noisy teenagers (and their friends) around, I was exhausted. But despite being bone tired, I had barely moved. I yearned, above all, for time on my own, for the chance to walk without interruption (and at the pace I chose), and for the silence of some empty wilderness. But I was nervous. Not of being on my own, but of what might happen to me with no one around to help (breaking a bone, encountering a psychopath, being chased by a bull, getting fatally lost). I could have found a companion or joined a group, but my need for silence and solitude outweighed my fears. Continue reading...

data.title: From influencers to brutal finishes, US Open 2026 was worst grand slam in recent memory | Tumaini Carayol
data.description: Despite the drama on the court, the poor condition of Arthur Ashe Stadium was just one problem among many At the end of another comically late night and early morning in Flushing Meadows, when the remaining spectators were departing, a familiar scene was unfolding on the US Open tournament grounds. A handful of workers had congregated directly beneath a hole in the ceiling inside one of the tournament shops as they tried to stop water from flowing out of a broken pipe and ruining thousands of pounds worth of merchandise below. This was not a surprising sight. Upon entering Arthur Ashe Stadium this year, fans were greeted by some ominous signs: “Pardon our appearance while we write the next chapter of Arthur Ashe Stadium.” The tournament’s appearance, it must be said, was hideous. Inside the corridors and rooms at one of the biggest sporting events in the world, it felt like its main building was falling apart. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Very weak. Very bad’: how Rodri’s verdict exposed woeful Valencia’s crisis | Sid Lowe
data.description: The World Cup winner’s off-the-cuff assessment was brutally honest. Within days their manager and CEO were gone, but the problems run much deeper Kiat Lim wanted to see Valencia play so badly, so that is what he did. It was week four in La Liga, 6 September, and for the first time since he was given the presidency 18 months earlier, the owner’s 33-year-old son was going to watch his team play a competitive game. He was going to do it from the inside, too, so he took a flight to Spain, landing at Manises in a black mask and cap, a van to the hotel, then the team bus to Mestalla. He looked through the window as they rolled along Avenida Suecia, a huge, noisy crowd waiting, but when he got off and headed through the iron gate with its ornate club badge, he saw that this was no welcome. Above him as he went in were giant portraits of Mario Kempes, Antonio Puchades, Juan Sol, Gaizka Mendieta, David Villa and Santiago Cañizares, footballers from a better time; around him were yellow banners and whistles for the footballers there now. Inside, Lim saw the game start with the lower south stand empty as fans stayed away until the 19th minute, the sound of another protest drifting in from the street. They were out there still when, sitting alongside Joan Laporta, he saw Lamine Yamal score the sixth-minute opener then get a second. And although that, also from Lamine Yamal, was ruled out, he eventually saw Barcelona get four more, presiding over a 5-0 debut defeat. Continue reading...

data.title: Polanski the first managerial victim of Bundesliga season as Gladbach fail again | Andy Brassell
data.description: Departure of head coach after defeat at Freiburg sums up club that could join other fallen giants in second tier It could not go on. Even at this early stage the sinking feeling was familiar and impossible to shake, and something had to give at Borussia Mönchengladbach. The first Bundesliga coaching change of the season is upon us just three games in, and it is not a major surprise that it is Eugen Polanski departing. Neither is it a shock that Gladbach are involved; after all, it was at exactly this point last season – three games in – that they parted ways with Gerardo Seoane. A club with more prospects and direction would have chosen to move on from Polanski in the summer, but the reality is that Gladbach have few of either. Saturday afternoon’s humiliation at Freiburg – a club enjoying a 100% record, guided by poise and purpose, having spent the Johan Manzambi money wisely – was no bad day at the office but a season in microcosm. The home side cruised into a 2-0 lead inside the first half-hour before the Gladbach captain, Tim Kleindienst, was sent off for a second yellow card (after an utterly avoidable first one). One former Gladbach player, Yannik Engelhardt, scored twice while another, Matthias Ginter, made two assists. It finished 5-0 and could have been way worse. Continue reading...

data.title: Sweden’s far right is down, but not yet out. Left and centre leaders must seize this opportunity | Cas Mudde
data.description: The danger is that other parties just channel the far right – and that will make them vulnerable. Better to fully commit to a progressive agenda After the previous Swedish general election, in 2022, the leaders of the two biggest Swedish parties made a risky decision. Jimmie Åkesson , the leader of the far-right Sweden Democrats (SD), chose to support the rightwing minority government of the Moderate party prime minister Ulf Kristersson , while Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrats’ leader, decided to copy the “Danish model” in an attempt to regain power. In both cases, the strategy led to electoral loss but political success . After the general election in the country on Sunday, the Social Democrats (often referred to as S or Sap), in common with its Danish counterparts, will probably lead the new government despite an electoral defeat, losing roughly 2%, its worst result since 1908. The party’s return to power is purely a result of Swedish bloc politics and the victories of its likely coalition partners : the Left party (V), the Green party and the Center party (C), which all increased their support by 1.5%, 1.7% and 0.4% respectively. Together, this left bloc has a majority of just three seats in the new parliament. So while Andersson will probably return to power, she is also in a very vulnerable position. Cas Mudde is the Stanley Wade Shelton UGAF professor of international affairs at the University of Georgia, and author of The Far Right Today Continue reading...

data.title: I’m a psychoanalyst. Social media is damaging children’s inner lives in ways we don’t fully understand | Robin Kirman
data.description: Discussion has focused on behavioral outcomes. But Meta’s settlement shines a light on damage to young people’s emerging desires and identities During the landmark social media addiction trial that led to Meta’s recent $17.1bn settlement , a therapist testified that she had once asked the plaintiff – a young woman named Kaley, who had been using social media since she was six – what her miracle day would look like: what she wished to come true, if anything were possible. Kaley replied that she would be prettier. As a psychoanalyst, I find that exchange devastating in a particular way. A miracle day is an invitation to engage with the full range of human desire: with what one might accomplish or experience, whom one might encounter or love. Kaley’s answer contracted the world and all its possibility into a single preoccupation with her own image. Continue reading...

data.title: The incoming ‘super’ El Niño will create chaos around the world. And we are far from ready for it | Bill McGuire
data.description: One of the biggest upheavals in a millennium is on its way, strengthened by the climate crisis. We need leaders who make things better not worse If you think you have heard enough about the growing “super” El Niño, trust me, you are going to hear a lot more. What is happening in the equatorial Pacific is jaw-dropping and could well mark one of the biggest global weather upheavals in a millennium. It will spawn a string of weather catastrophes around our world in what remains of this year and in 2027, and there is no reason to think the UK will be immune. To recap briefly, El Niño involves a heating of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific ocean. It happens every few years and is part of a natural cycle termed the El Niño southern oscillation, which switches between warm (El Niño) and cool (La Niña) phases. El Niños that see heating reach or exceed 2C are defined as “super” but this one, which is forecast to top-out at an astonishing 4C later this year, is so much bigger, the term “hyper” might be more appropriate. Bill McGuire is professor emeritus of geophysical and climate hazards at UCL. His latest book is The Fate of the World: A History and Future of the Climate Crisis Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Reform UK: crypto billionaires must be stopped from undermining democracy | Editorial
data.description: The vast sums given to Nigel Farage’s party in recent days must lead to action on political funding The staggering sums gifted to Reform UK over the weekend have transformed the context for the representation of the people bill making its way through parliament. The announcement of two £36m donations from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, both crypto billionaires who have lived abroad, makes Andy Burnham’s decision not to impose a limit on political donations – a move he supported before becoming prime minister – look even more misguided. Fortunately the House of Lords still has the chance to amend the bill. It should take it by imposing meaningful limits on both political donations and party spending. It is unclear whether either man meets the criteria set out in the Rycroft review into foreign influence in politics. It set a maximum of £100,000 per annum for people who have not been in the UK for at least a year. Mr Delo previously lived in Hong Kong while Mr Harborne is based partly in Thailand; Nigel Farage said on Monday that he does not know the details of their movements. While ministers will view the prospect of a legal fight over eligibility with trepidation, they must do what it takes to ensure rules are met. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the united Ireland debate: shifting dynamics need to be treated with caution | Editorial
data.description: Donald Trump’s blithe comments at the weekend were characteristically unhelpful. A careful and considered discussion on the subject  has yet to begin A decade ago, the Democratic Unionist party (DUP) viewed Brexit as a potential gamechanger in the struggle to resist future pressure for a united Ireland. As the author and journalist Fintan O’Toole wrote in an essay published last year, the DUP hoped that the 2016 referendum would deliver “a double exit. Brexit would not simply mean the UK’s departure from the EU. It would also be an act of separation from the Republic. It would reverse the slow drift towards integration.” That proved to be, to put it mildly, a deeply flawed judgment. The direction of travel since 2016 has instead been the opposite. Rather than leading to a hard border between Northern Ireland and Ireland, which would have disastrously undermined the Good Friday agreement, the UK’s divorce agreement from Brussels eventually placed one in the Irish Sea. The logic of further economic integration between north and south within the EU’s single market was reinforced. Continue reading...

data.title: Farage says a Reform UK government would stop unions funding Labour if they block £72m donations – UK politics live
data.description: Party leader claims proposed new retrospective laws are unfair and Reform would retaliate with a crackdown on union funding if elected Jonathan Reynolds has said that people should not get “hyperbolic” about the risks posed by AI. Speaking ahead of Louise Haigh’s speech to the TUC later, which will address the topic (see 9.31am ), and in the light of the ongoing concerns expressed by AI experts about the risk of AI models posing a threat to humanity, Reynolds told the Today programme: This is extremely powerful technology, and I think we should never be complacent or naive about the impact it might have. People will be worried by some of the things they’ve heard in the last few weeks, and I think we’ve got to be careful not to get hyperbolic about this either. Because of the power of this technology, I wouldn’t say I wasn’t worried. What I would say is I’m clear-eyed about the best ways to keep the country safe, and that has to be using British innovation, British expertise, British specialisms in such a way that actually improves the position of the UK in terms of the safety. I’ve got to be honest, I don’t think that it’s a particularly helpful way to think about how we manage the risks. I’m not really sure what that would actually mean in practice. To state the obvious, these frontier models are in the main being developed in the US and in China. So exactly what would that mean? I’m not sure what the proposition is. When we talk, or people talk about union donations, that is not one entity. That is tens of thousands of ordinary people choosing to make that donation, and it’s bundled up and given from the union. But it’s very easy to opt out of that. There are rules governing political funds, political ballots. I honestly think to take these mega, ultra crypto Reform donors and compare them to voluntary associations of working people choosing to give some money to the political system, I don’t think the two things are comparable. Continue reading...

data.title: They’re the sopranos of the forest, so what’s silencing the gibbons’ morning chorus?
data.description: As human development and roads increasingly fragment their habitats, a study suggests traffic noise could be altering the animals’ wake-up call Dawn has broken, and the air is cool and still. It’s at about this time that gibbons usually erupt into song, wa-oo-ing and wa-ing from the highest branches and filling the tree tops with rich melodies. But in this corner of Malaysian forest, bordered by housing and roads, the resident white-handed gibbons are quiet. All that can be heard is the hum of traffic from a nearby highway. This isn’t a rare occurrence for this group of gibbons, according to research, which found these particular gibbons, named Mambang and Walinong, appeared to be producing far fewer morning songs than others that are not exposed to the same level of traffic noise. data.title: Conservation ‘gateway drug’: farmers embrace ancient craft of hedge laying
data.description: Grant applications in England surge as interest grows in habitat that captures carbon and helps reduce flood risk The ancient craft of hedge laying is experiencing a strong revival as farmers use techniques that peaked in the 18th and 19th centuries to boost wildlife, capture carbon and help tackle flooding. Hedge laying, which restores and revives mature hedges to keep them fresh, was among the four most popular categories of capital grants selected by farmers out of a total pot of £225m provided by the government this year to support practical environmental improvements on farms and across the countryside. data.title: ‘Carbon fever’ threatens hard-won Indigenous rights in Bolivian Amazon
data.description: Leaders in Pando region denounce opaque deals over carbon credits as government and companies rush to monetise Amazon rainforest after 2024 ruling In the village plazas of Pando, a remote northern Amazonian region of Bolivia, the main talk is no longer just about the next harvest. One pressing issue is the “invisible air” being sold to foreigners who regularly visit their communities. In June 2024, the country’s constitutional court struck down the ban on a funding mechanism linked to carbon markets. Since then, Indigenous leaders of three ethnic groups – the Tacana, Ese Ejja and Cabineño – have complained about companies and foundations that arrive with offers of “climate solutions”, often during the ever more frequent droughts or floods. Continue reading...

data.title: US ‘super-emitters’ of planet heating methane identified by satellite analysis
data.description: Energy Transfer, whose CEO is a major Trump donor, named as biggest single methane producer in new rankings Down a short gravel track in a largely nondescript corner of Louisiana sits a gas processing facility, operated by a company whose chief executive is a major donor to Donald Trump. It may be the largest emitter of methane in the US. The Energy Transfer site, located near the city of Shreveport, is named as the biggest single “super emitter” in new rankings of US oil and gas operations for the largest releases of methane, a powerful greenhouse gas that is rapidly overheating our planet, according to a new UCLA study, which is based on satellite data. Continue reading...

data.title: Why unwanted fridges are piling up at recycling centres across England and Wales
data.description: Capacity has been overwhelmed by heatwaves that have pushed white goods to breaking point “In Oxfordshire, recycling centres are filling almost three articulated lorries with discarded fridges every week,” says Simon Perry of W&S Waste Management, which runs a recycling centre in Ardley. Together, those fridges would cover an area just under half the size of a football pitch. But the space to store them – in Oxfordshire and beyond – has become a growing problem after the Local Government Association (LGA) warned that a mountain of broken fridges was rising in waste centres across England and Wales, as this year’s heatwaves push more white goods to breaking point, and a trend for second/backup refrigeration products keeps growing. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Signs of violence’: asylum seekers arriving in France injured after being deported from UK
data.description: French health service documents injuries including fractures and bruising after detention and return under ‘one in one out’ scheme Multiple injuries including bruising and fractures have been documented by a health service supporting people returned to France under the controversial “one in, one out” scheme. The pilot scheme involves one asylum seeker who crosses the Channel in a small boat being returned to France in return for another in northern France being legally brought to the UK to claim asylum. The scheme is due to end on 1 October . Continue reading...

data.title: Digital ID comes of age as pubs and bars get go-ahead for biometric scan tech
data.description: New laws coming into force this week aim to streamline age checks although old-style plastic IDs will still be allowed Younger drinkers in England and Wales will be able to prove their age with a digital ID starting this week as new laws give pubs, off-licences, nightclubs and restaurants the right to use biometric scanning technology to check customers are over 18. Customers will be able to download software that scans their faces into their own phone to generate a QR code proving their age based on a stored proof of age. Other tech under consideration as part of the government push to digitise age verification for alcohol sales include a device which scans the veins in a drinker’s finger to verify their age. That system has not yet been approved for use. Continue reading...

data.description: Alistair Burt speaks candidly about difficulties of tackling complex cases as families express concern over mandate The special envoy for British citizens detained overseas has spoken about the difficulties he faces in his new role, as families express concern over the position’s mandate in complex consular cases. In his first public engagement, Alistair Burt , the former Conservative Middle East minister, spoke candidly about the difficulties and limitations of the new appointment, made following years of mounting criticism of how the Foreign Office handled the cases of British citizens detained overseas. data.title: Australia’s Indigenous population estimated at 2.2m before ‘demographic catastrophe’ of colonisation
data.description: Study finds earlier numbers were underestimated, suggesting impact of diseases and massacres were much greater than previously thought Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Australia before colonisation was dramatically underestimated, according to new research that suggests many more of them were killed. Modelling by a national research group puts the population levels before the 1788 first fleet arrived at 2.2 million, compared with early estimates of 250,000 people. Continue reading...

data.description: Neck-and-neck with Lula in polls, Flávio Bolsonaro fires up his base in the bellwether state of Minas Gerais – starting at the scene of his father’s stabbing A giant banner of Brazil’s incarcerated former president Jair Bolsonaro fluttered in the morning breeze as his eldest son, Flávio, touched down at an airfield on the fringe of a city that will soon help decide the future of one of the biggest democracies on earth. “Brazil is rudderless. data.title: Oasis announce 2027 tour, including return to Knebworth 30 years after historic concerts
data.description: After 2025’s wildly lucrative reunion, the Gallagher brothers will tour the UK, Ireland and US, and revisit the Hertfordshire site of their greatest live triumph • From the archive: How did the Guardian cover Oasis at Knebworth 1996? Well … we didn’t Oasis have finally confirmed new tour dates for 2027, including their long-rumoured return to Knebworth for a run of shows 30 years after they played a historic two nights at the Hertfordshire venue in 1996. “Start the celebrations!”, the band said in a statement. “After a period of reflection, The Most Damaging Pop Cultural Force in Recent British History” – a quote from a Guardian opinion piece about the band – “has declared itself fit for purpose and will once again return to lift the spirits of the people. data.title: Ancestors review – messy but moving ghostly drama about the Aids crisis
data.description: Toronto film festival: Saipan standout Éanna Hardwicke is a soulful gay man looking for a missing friend in a striking yet muddled debut It’s not normal to regularly contemplate mortality in your twenties, to ask questions about where we might go after we die and whether any part of our legacy will even matter in the years following. But for gay men in the 1980s, death was everywhere. In David Turpin’s intermittently impactful debut Ancestors, the director tries to make a connection with those men who lived through the very worst years of the Aids crisis. Turpin, born in 1982, might not have the first-hand experience but he bears the scars passed on from generation to generation and like many young gay men coming of age in the years after, likely experienced a watered down version of the shame and fear those before him once felt. Continue reading...

data.title: Night of the Coyotes review – border-crossing role-play is tourist attraction in struggling Mexican town
data.description: Clara Trischler’s absorbing feature sees residents of the small town of El Alberto hired to play characters in a re-enactment of the migrant experience In contrast to other migration documentaries, which focus on the new life that awaits those who have crossed the border, Clara Trischler’s absorbing second feature trains its gaze on those who are left behind. The suspenseful opening plunges us into a whirl of familiar images: tense whispers in the dead of night as a ragtag group of people stumble, and even crawl, their way towards an unseen border. All of a sudden a blinding light intrudes, guns are fired in the air: a police car has arrived on the scene. This terrifying sequence of events is later revealed to be make-believe. In the small Mexican town of El Alberto, whose population has been depleted by a steady flow of migration to the US, role-playing re-enactments function as both a means of deterrent and, oddly enough, a tourist attraction. Advertised as Caminata Nocturna – “night hike” in Spanish – these events recruit local residents to perform as specific characters, including the fearsome “coyotes”, AKA human traffickers. The attendees experience the full scale of a border-crossing operation, from being loaded on vans to intimidation from their coyotes, and police interrogation. Continue reading...

data.title: Premature review – sunny charm provides screwball energy for surprise-pregnancy comedy
data.description: First-time director Kevin Walls creates a film sweet-natured enough to cancel out some comedy misfires as flatmates Eilidh and Cameron prepare for parenthood The pram in the hallway is the enemy of good art, or so the famous quote goes . This sunny Scottish comedy, made on a minuscule budget, deals with the bit before the pram, when an art school dropout in her 20s gets unexpectedly up the duff. It’s directed by first-timer Kevin Walls, who gives his film the screwball-ish energy of things being skew-whiffly the wrong way round; a couple are going on their first date at three months pregnant, having a baby at an age most people are putting it off to establish their careers. It’s sweet-natured with just about enough charm to cancel out a couple of thunderously awful comedy moments. Elle Watson is artist Eilidh, who works as a barista in a museum cafe. She has a friends-with-benefits setup with her flatmate Cameron (James Rottger); he has a job in finance and, after two degrees, a mountain of student debt and years in a mind-numbing entry-level position, he’s finally lined up an interview for his dream job. It would be crazy to have the baby, but Eilidh doesn’t take the abortion tablets. She can’t give Cameron a coherent reason why not; fair enough, it’s her decision, a gut feeling. Walls sensibly doesn’t go anywhere near the pro-choice/anti-abortion debate. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The eye-gouging was very, very satisfying’: how we made cave horror classic The Descent
data.description: ‘The child crawler whose head I crush with my boot was only 11, bless him. It was actually me stamping on a cauliflower’ I was introduced to Christian Colson at Celador Films off the back of [2002 horror film] Dog Soldiers, and I pitched them a project – actually a feature-length version of my student graduation film – about zombies on an oil rig. They liked it but said it was too expensive, so on the train back to Newcastle I was asking myself what would make a really scary horror film that could be contained and so made on a budget. I was thinking of things set in the dark and was like, well … caves . At the back of my mind was a school trip to a lead mine where the guide had said, “OK, everybody, turn your lights off” and, for the first time, I experienced a darkness that I just couldn’t fathom. Continue reading...

data.title: Beck: Ride Lonesome review – stunning end to the heartache trilogy of Sea Change and Morning Phase
data.description: (Iliad/Capitol) On his first album in seven years, Beck keeps the quality control extremely high as he surveys mid-50s malaise in the wake of divorce The last time Beck released an album it was 2019 and the singer-songwriter found himself in a strange and unenviable position. In some quarters, the arrival of Hyperspace was eagerly anticipated precisely because his personal life was in turmoil. Nine months before its release, his 15-year marriage to actor Marissa Ribisi had ended in divorce, an experience he understandably described as heartbreaking. Unfortunately for him, there exists a pervasive argument that Beck’s greatest work is born out of misery. His beloved 2002 album Sea Change featured a set of disconsolate acoustic songs written in the wake of a break-up with his long-term girlfriend Leigh Limon that Beck had initially thought were too personal for public consumption. They were certainly very different from the knowing, postmodern approach with which he’d made his name, but no matter: Sea Change went on to become a huge critical and commercial success. It wasn’t entirely clear what prompted the gloomy mood of 2014’s Morning Phase, but it very much seemed to be cut from similar musical and lyrical cloth. Some critics suggested it was the best album of his career; it subsequently won three Grammys, including album of the year. Given the circumstances, there was much pre-release speculation that Hyperspace would be a companion piece. Continue reading...

data.title: The Rouse by China Miéville review – a mighty achievement from the ‘new weird’ author
data.description: Twenty years in the writing, this paranormal epic of cold war espionage and family tragedy is a quantum leap in terms of ambition and moral seriousness China Miéville’s epic new novel is presented as being “20 years in the making”. It is quite a testament to how extravagant – even Stakhanovite – his imagination is that during that period he also produced six novels (including The City & the City and The Book of Elsewhere , co-written with Keanu Reeves), two novellas, two series of graphic novels, a children’s book, a volume of short stories and two works of nonfiction, on the October Revolution and the Communist Manifesto. It does not mean that these works were, as Graham Greene called The Third Man and Our Man in Havana, “entertainments” – Embassytown , to my mind, is the best translation of deconstructionist philosophy into science fiction – but certainly The Rouse is a quantum jump in terms of ambition, moral seriousness and stylistic bravado. It means that rather than classifying Miéville with “the new weird” or “speculative fantasy”, he ought to be compared to Roberto Bolaño or Mircea Cărtărescu. This new novel is equally maximalist, dense, disorienting and discomfiting, reflecting how surreal our reality seems to have become. Continue reading...

data.title: In an age of superhero fatigue, Marvel’s best shot is to think small – and outside the box
data.description: Sebastian Stan says he pitched Marvel a mid-budget thriller starring his Winter Soldier character. Perhaps the studio should give it – and other modestly scaled vehicles – the green light Blink a little and you might think we are back in 2019. The latest Spider-Man film, Brand New Day, has just passed $2.4bn at the global box office, to become the third-highest grossing film of all time behind Avatar and Avengers: Endgame. Meanwhile Avengers: Doomsday is reported to have already earned more than $50m in US ticket presales alone, despite the fact that it doesn’t come out until December. Clearly we are in the middle of a superhero renaissance. And yet it doesn’t really feel like it, largely because it is something of a turnaround for Marvel, after a pretty disappointing 2025 in which all three of the studio’s releases underperformed. Captain America: Brave New World took $415m worldwide, Thunderbolts* managed $382m and even the well-reviewed The Fantastic Four: First Steps stalled at $521m, against a reported $200m budget. These are hardly Madame Web numbers but they do suggest there is still a problem about what to do with all those superheroes who cannot sustain a $300m multiversal extravaganza. Continue reading...

data.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the rat who jumped off the wardrobe and flew at my face
data.description: There was a rat army in my flatshare, gnawing through pipes, carpets and even a bedroom door. That’s not to mention the mice ... We should have known we were in trouble when we saw that the garden of our new place backed on to a Chinese restaurant in Hackney, London, with terrible reviews. Before long, the rats started coming in through the pipes. It was ratmageddon, and every day it got more harrowing. They trooped over our kitchen, like the world’s worst sequel to Ratatouille. They calmly walked into rooms while we were watching telly. They gnawed through all the carpets to try to get into our bedrooms. There was no stopping them. After sniffing out the remnants of an old snack in my housemate Simon’s bin, a pack of rats got to work one night gnawing through the wood at the bottom of his bedroom door. Like a rodent military exercise, they spent eight hours whittling a hole large enough to get through. I lay next door, 100% freaked out, panicking they’d try to get into my room next. I didn’t sleep a wink. Fairly soon after this, one of the rats died under the floorboards so we got a bottle-fly infestation to boot. Naturally, our landlord did nothing about any of this. Continue reading...

data.title: Rosie Mackean’s quick and easy recipe for lamb chops with courgettes, walnuts and yoghurt | Quick and easy
data.description: Intimidated by the thought of midweek entertaining? Three simple rules make it simple… Entertaining midweek can feel daunting, but if you employ a couple of tricks, things can very quickly go from mayhem to magic. First, choose a dish that goes perfectly with good bread, so your carb is covered. Second, choose a protein that is quick to cook and great for sharing – little lamb chops are perfect for this, while also being a treat. And, finally, use other ingredients that don’t need much help. Here, the walnuts just get cooked in butter and the lamb juices, the courgettes are simply boiled and dressed, and the yoghurt is, well, yoghurt. data.description: The hormone-packed pothos plant might encourage healthy root growth in other cuttings – or it might not. This is often attributed to pothos releasing auxins – the plant hormones involved in root development – into the shared water. Continue reading...

data.title: The one change that worked: I was terrified of the dentist – until I found a very special one
data.description: After an agonising experience, I avoided checkups for four years. But a practice that assured a stress-free process for scared patients was transformative I haven’t always been afraid of the dentist. If you had asked me a decade ago whether sitting in the dentist’s chair filled me with dread or made me break out in a cold sweat, I would have laughed and said no – what is there to be afraid of? It was only in 2021, after I had a filling without being properly numbed, that I understood why people are afraid of dental work. Despite telling him I was in excruciating pain, the dentist carried on with the procedure anyway, and I was left with a newfound and deep-seated fear. At first, this was easily managed. I simply binned the reminders to book checkups, avoided their calls and carried on with my life. After a year, I told myself I’d see the dentist soon – just not yet. I firmly shoved the problem to the back of my mind. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: No energy ceasefire until Russia stops, Zelenskyy confirms after Trump claim
data.description: Moscow would need to commit ‘honestly and on a long-term basis’ to peace before Kyiv would de-escalate. What we know on day 1,665 Ukraine will only halt attacks on Russian energy targets if the enemy does likewise and the US guarantees it, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The announcement came after Donald Trump’s uncorroborated claim that both sides have agreed to such a ceasefire. Neither Ukraine nor Russia had said so at time of writing. The US president regularly claims to have brokered what turn out to be nonexistent or extremely shortlived deals between foreign adversaries or with his own overseas enemies, such as Iran. Ukraine’s president said: “So far, no one ‌has seen any genuine ‌willingness on Russia’s part to bring the war to an end. But if our ‌American partners can secure Russia’s genuine readiness to end the war aimed at destroying lives, and to do so honestly and on a long-term basis, Ukraine will take its own de-escalatory steps.” Russia would need to stop attacking Ukraine’s critical infrastructure for its intentions to be taken seriously, Zelenskyy suggested. It comes after Trump tried to blame diesel shortages and high prices on Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries. The main cause is Trump’s own war on Iran – the retaliation for which has crippled the trade in Middle East oil. Russia has banned diesel exports to address dire shortages at home caused by Ukraine’s attacks. But those exports comprise only a fraction of global supply , and the situation most directly affects neighbouring countries such as those in central Asia like Mongolia that rely heavily on supplies from Russian producers. A ⁠Nato fighter jet shot down a drone in Lithuania shortly after ⁠midnight on Tuesday, ⁠the national crisis management centre said. The drone, which likely entered from Belarus , ⁠was shot down near Pratkunai village in southern Lithuania, near Kaunas, the second-largest city, ⁠the centre’s spokesperson said. Its origin was yet ​to be determined at time of writing. A ‌drone alert was issued earlier in the ‌capital, Vilnius, and surrounding region. A ⁠Russian attack on ⁠a farming warehouse killed three people in the ⁠town ​of Pryluky ‌in Ukraine’s ‌northern Chernihiv ‌region, regional police said. Seven ​others were injured. Prosecutors in Germany have charged a German-Ukrainian woman with acting on behalf of Russian intelligence. The woman, identified as Ilona W in line with German privacy rules, is accused of being in contact with an intelligence officer at the Russian embassy in Berlin since at least October 2023. The defendant ran a marketing agency in Berlin and chaired a lobbying group, using these networks to get the intelligence officer into high-profile events, and to try to recruit German defence officials and industry figures. A member of the UK armed forces was killed in a crash in Ukraine on Saturday, Britain’s defence ministry said. It is understood the incident was not a result of hostile action, writes Priya Bharadia . A small number of British personnel in Ukraine provide security to diplomats and support the Ukrainian armed forces. Volodymyr Zelenskyy has formally dismissed Ukraine’s prosecutor general, Ruslan Kravchenko, whose office is embroiled in a bribery scandal. Zelenskyy announced the sacking in a government decree. Kravchenko – who has denied the allegations, but resigned on 7 September – posted that he is now outside Ukraine and has started legal action against the head of the national anti-corruption bureau, Nabu, accusing him of “falsifying official documents”. Nabu investigators raided the prosecutor general’s offices and said they had uncovered a network that made payments in return for protecting fraudulent call centres that had “laundered fortunes”. Continue reading...

data.title: O Supremo é um risco à democracia?
data.description: O Brasil se defrontará com a verdade nesta terça (15). Nada garante que ela será abonadora. Eu preservo uma ponta de esperança de que uma maioria de ministros cumprirá o mínimo dever de justiça e abrirá o inquérito contra Alexandre de Moraes . Lembremos que, mesmo com todos os seus tentáculos milionários, Vorcaro está preso. Seu banco foi fechado e diversas autoridades estão sob investigação. Há instituições que funcionam. Falta à Justiça adentrar a última cidadela da impunidade. O Supremo e seus ministros -alguns mais do que outros- acostumaram-se a mandar no Brasil. Quando, em 2022, um site de jornalismo publicou que empresários num grupo privado de WhatsApp disseram que preferiam um golpe à vitória de Lula , Moraes não teve dúvida: apreendeu seus celulares, quebrou seus sigilos telefônicos, bloqueou suas contas bancárias e redes sociais. Contra Moraes há dezenas de milhões de reais, viagens de jatinho, mensagens inexplicáveis. Quando Moraes era juiz, o fato de " Débora do batom " ter apagado mensagens de seu celular apenas reforçava sua culpa. Com Moraes sob suspeita, ele ter feito a mesma coisa dificulta o singelo pedido de investigá-lo; afinal, não sabemos se ele respondeu ao ex-banqueiro. Leia mais (09/14/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Från uselt till glädjetårar – så vände hon Liberalerna
data.description: Liberalerna var fullkomligt uträknade. Partiet kämpade med usla opinionssiffror och uppslitande interna bråk när den oprövade Simona Mohamsson tog över. Hennes kram med Jimmie Åkesson såg inte ut att hjälpa partiet, tvärtom. Men genom en historisk upphämtning har hon nu räddat kvar Liberalerna i riksdagen. Hur gick det egentligen till? Programledare: Elinor Ahlborn. Med Patrik Lundberg, reporter på DN. Producent: Måns Mosesson.

data.title: Cyberterroryzm – nowe zagrożenie, które wymaga nowych specjalistów
data.description: Jeden złośliwy skrypt potrafi w kilka sekund odciąć od zasilania całe miasto, sparaliżować pracę szpitali lub wyczyścić konta bankowe tysięcy ludzi. Ataki w sieci przestały być domeną pojedynczych hakerów szukających rozgłosu, a stały się bezwzględną bronią w rękach zorganizowanych grup przestępczych. Prawie każdego dnia słyszysz o wyciekach poufnych danych, zablokowanych systemach logistycznych oraz włamaniach do serwerów rządowych. Cyfrowa przestrzeń przekształciła się w pełnoprawne pole walki, gdzie stawką jest stabilność państwa i bezpieczeństwo milionów obywateli. Zrozumienie natury tego zjawiska pozwala uświadomić sobie, jak gwałtownie rośnie zapotrzebowanie na ludzi potrafiących skutecznie neutralizować wrogie operacje.

data.title: AfD má v celoněmeckém průzkumu poprvé 30 procent, Merzově CDU dál utíká
data.description: Alternativa pro Německo (AfD) poprvé v některém z průzkumů k celoněmeckým volbám dosáhla podpory 30 procent. Před Křesťanskodemokratickou unií (CDU) kancléře Friedricha Merze, která je druhá, má podle agentury GMS náskok deset procentních bodů. Další dva průzkumy, které vyšly dnes, připisují AfD 29 procent a uvádějí ji rovněž na prvním místě. Strana předminulý týden vyhrála zemské volby v Sasku-Anhaltsku a vyhrát by mohla i nedělní volby v Meklenbursku-Předním Pomořansku. Ve volbách v Berlíně by mohla zisk zdvojnásobit.

data.title: Zlomové oznámení. USA mají zbraně na oběžné dráze, potvrdily vesmírné síly
data.description: Spojené státy disponují zbraněmi rozmístěnými po oběžné dráze, uvedly v pondělí americké vesmírné síly, složka amerických ozbrojených sil zaměřená na vesmírné bojiště. data.title: KOMENTÁŘ: Odstraňování „metastáz“ se daří. Moskvu rozpad Velké Británie potěší
data.description: Memorandu lídrů Skotska, Severního Irska a Walesu o právu jejich národů na sebeurčení a tedy odchodu z Velké Británie, mohou v Rusku mocně tleskat. Není pro Moskvu důležité, že tyto země svou budoucnost vidí v Evropské unii, do které by se po svízelných přístupových jednáních stejně mohly dostat až za mnoho let. Důležitý je rozklad jednoho z nejnenáviděnějších ruských soků.

data.title: ANALÝZA: Miliardové investice evropských hutí do dekarbonizace? Podmínky dál chybějí
data.description: Evropské ocelářství vstupuje do období, kdy má současně zvládnout drahé energie, tlak levných dovozů a investice do zásadního snížení emisí. Evropská unie proto postupně upravuje několik klíčových nástrojů – systém emisních povolenek EU ETS, uhlíkové vyrovnání na hranicích CBAM i ochranu trhu před nadměrnými dovozy.

data.title: Pacientka odešla z psychiatrie, nezvěstná je už dva týdny. Rodina nabízí odměnu
data.description: Policie a rodina zatím marně pátrají po třiašedesátileté ženě z Uherskohradišťska. Jitka Lukašíková odešla z psychiatrické léčebny v Kroměříži v úterý 2. září. Policie po ní vyhlásila pátrání o den později, zatím bez výsledku. Podle svědků byla počátkem měsíce pravděpodobně spatřena na Frenštátsku. Nešťastná rodina vyhlásila za nalezení ženy odměnu 200 tisíc korun.

data.title: Vedení Brna chce schválit prodej stadionu Zbrojovce, poruší tím ale zákon
data.description: Zákonům to sice odporuje, což ale v Brně očividně nevadí. Zastupitelé města na dnešním jednání od devíti hodin rozhodují o tom, jestli i navzdory zákonným postupům schválí prodej zchátralého stadionu za Lužánkami majiteli brněnské fotbalové Zbrojovky Vojtěchu Kačenovi. Ten tam chce pro klub postavit zbrusu nový stánek za vlastní peníze.

data.title: Poláka na charitativní jízdě zbili v Ostravě. Zřejmě krajané kvůli „ukrajinské“ hučce
data.description: Policie v Ostravě vyšetřuje napadení Poláka Jakuba Heisiga, který kvůli utrpěným zraněním přerušil charitativní jízdu na kole česko-polským pohraničím. Napadený tvrdí, že na něj nejspíše zaútočili polští krajané kvůli tomu, že měl žluto-modrý klobouček. To jsou však barvy nejen Ukrajiny, ale také historické země Horní Slezsko.

data.title: Brit dvacet let omamoval a znásilňoval manželku, pozval si i třináct dalších mužů
data.description: Muž ve Velké Británii více než dvacet let podával své manželce omamné látky a znásilňoval ji. Šedesátiletý Brit se k tomu v pondělí přiznal před soudem. Obžalovaný se zároveň přiznal k šedesáti trestným činům sahajícím až do roku 2004, včetně podání látky s úmyslem omámit nebo znehybnit manželku.

data.title: V prostějovském parku ležel mrtvý muž. Násilnou smrt policie nakonec vyloučila

data.title: Panamský průplav dále omezuje provoz. El Niño ještě neřeklo své poslední slovo
data.description: Panamský průplav plánuje další omezení námořního provozu. Nejnovější krok tak ještě více zúží jednu z nejdůležitějších námořních tras světa. Průplav zajišťuje pět procent celosvětového námořního obchodu a přibližně 40 procent kontejnerové přepravy z USA. Přepravci jej upřednostňují, neboť tato trasa obvykle snižuje náklady a zkracuje přepravní časy, zejména pro společnosti obchodující mezi Čínou, Asií a Spojenými státy.

data.title: Čelní střet náklaďáku a auta na Brněnsku. Spolujezdkyně zemřela, řidička je zraněná

data.title: Ruský podnikatel spojený s Kremlem zaplatil oslavy po svatbě Trumpova syna

data.title: Arepa Fest: dos días para celebrar una memoria que se come con las manos
data.description: La actividad celebró durante dos días, en la terraza del Centro Comercial Parque Cerro Verde, el Día Mundial de la Arepa. La expectativa de superar las 20.000 visitas contrastó con una afluencia menor que la registrada en 2025. data.title: Coupe de la Confédération : Durban City éteint Rukinzo et poursuit son songe continental
data.description:
1er tour préliminaire retour de la Coupe de la CAF. 
 Il n’a fallu que 32 secondes pour que l’histoire bascule. 
 Sous le ciel de Bujumbura, au Stade Intwari le 13 septembre 2026, Durban City n’est pas venu négocier. Il est venu conclure. Et il l’a fait avec la froide élégance des équipes qui savent où elles vont. 
 Victoire 1-2 face à Rukinzo FC. Qualification validée sur un score cumulé de 3-1. Les hommes de Khalil Ben Youssef avancent. Et le rêve se poursuit.

data.title: Cameroun : Hadja Haoua, Mgr Bala, Martinez Zogo, le syndrome de « l’enquête ouverte » qui n’aboutit jamais ?
data.description: © DR La même phrase revient depuis 9 ans au Cameroun : "Une enquête a été ouverte". C'est la même angoisse qui revient avec l'affaire Hadja Haoua, portée par une association de Garoua. Le 14 septembre 2026, l'Association pour la défense des droits des opprimés -ADDO- saisit Paul Biya pour une disparue : dame Hadja Haoua. Connue comme une militante du Rassemblement démocratiques du peuple camerounais-RDPC- de Yaoundé, et pour ses vidéos virales en "Mondovision" où elle s'attaquait à de hauts responsables. Mais depuis, plus aucun signe de vie. C'est là que l'ADDO sort l'artillerie lourde : elle cite l'écrivaine Calixthe Beyala qui aurait affirmé que "son corps a été jeté d'un hélicoptère au-dessus de la forêt de Bertoua". Vrai ? Faux ? Rumeur ? L'ADDO elle-même pose la question : "Quel crédit peut-on accorder à ce témoignage troublant, mais combien récurrent ?" Et l’organisation fait le lien qui fait froid dans le dos avec deux affaires que les Camerounais n'ont jamais digérées. Mgr Jean-Marie Benoît Bala - 31 mai 2017 L'Evêque de Bafia, Mgr Benoît Bala , retrouvé mort dans la Sanaga, au fond de l'eau. Dans sa voiture, une lettre d'adieu jugée douteuse par ses proches. La thèse officielle : noyade/ suicide. La thèse de la famille et de l'Eglise : assassinat. L'enquête ? Annoncée, puis silence radio. 9 ans après, toujours aucune vérité judiciaire. "Monseigneur s'est retrouvé au fond du lac à l'instar d'un poisson d'eau douce, prenant prétendument soin d'orienter sa dernière demeure à travers une pseudo-lettre abandonnée dans sa voiture", écrit l'ADDO. Martinez Zogo - 17 janvier 2023 Le chef de chaine de la radio Amplitude FM, enlevé, torturé, son corps mutilé retrouvé à Ebogo. L'affaire qui a fait trembler la République avec l'inculpation du patron de la DGRE Léopold Maxime Eko Eko et du magnat Jean-Pierre Amougou Belinga. Procès fleuve, mais 3 ans après, toujours pas de jugement définitif. Le nom des commanditaires présumés circule, mais la justice peine. L'ADDO s’inquiète pour Haoua et fait le rapprochement. "Elle ne donne aucun signe de vie... si elle n'est pas dans l'œil du cyclone dans le prolongement du sillon labial, de feu Martinez Zogo ." Hadja Haoua - Septembre 2026 C'est le maillon manquant. Selon l'ADDO, Hadja Haoua aurait "beaucoup vu, beaucoup entendu" en haut lieu en tant que ‘’épouse de M. Baongla, présenté comme fils aîné présumé du Président’’. Elle aurait "violé leurs secrets intimes" en direct sur Facebook. L'association admet : ses propos étaient "orduriers", "téméraires", "condamnables" pour injures publiques. Mais elle pose la question centrale d'un Etat de droit : "Ses parents ont le droit de savoir sous quel toit réside leur fille, quelle est la sentence retenue contre elle et pourquoi ?" Au mieux, dit-elle, "internée dans les geôles d'infortune". Au pire, "jetée dans la tombe". Le plus important pour eux d’abord de savoir où elle se trouve. Le point commun : la formule magique Pour l'ADDO, le mode opératoire semble identique : "L'enquête ouverte est désormais un terme usité chaque fois pour la clôturer définitivement ce jour même pour mettre fin à toutes investigations... pour ranger les dossiers compromettants dans les placards de l'indulgence condamnable et l'impunité abjecte." C'est ce que l'association appelle le "kidnapping d'Etat" et le "gangstérisme indécent qui prospère en raison du mutisme complice et aberrant et de l'autoritarisme excédent". data.translatedDescription: © DR La même phrase revient depuis 9 ans au Cameroun : "Une enquête a été ouverte". data.title: Cameroun/ IRAD : la spectroscopie infrarouge au service des sols
data.description: © DR Du 14 au 18 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé, l'IRAD organise son École thématique 2026 sur « La spectroscopie infrarouge appliquée aux sciences du sol ». Une vingtaine de chercheurs et ingénieurs du Cameroun et du Gabon formés pour une gestion durable des sols. C'est une montée en compétences stratégique pour la recherche agronomique. Sous le thème « La spectroscopie infrarouge appliquée aux sciences du sol », l'Institut de Recherche Agricole pour le Développement (IRAD) tient du 14 au 18 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé, l'édition 2026 de son École thématique. Cette formation, d'un grand intérêt pour la connaissance et la gestion durable des sols, réunit une vingtaine de chercheurs et ingénieurs de l'IRAD, de l'IITA, et des Universités d'Etat du Cameroun et du Gabon. Animé par des experts de haut vol, l'atelier offre un enseignement théorique et pratique permettant d'acquérir et de renforcer les connaissances dans le domaine de la spectroscopie infrarouge appliquée à l'étude et à la caractérisation des sols. La cérémonie d'ouverture a été présidée par le DGA chargé de la Recherche Scientifique de l'IRAD, le Dr Francis NGOME. Cet article Cameroun/ IRAD : la spectroscopie infrarouge au service des sols est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Youth Connekt Cameroon : le privé appelé à amplifier la phase 2
data.description: © DR A Douala le 10 septembre 2026, le Ministre Mounouna Foutsou a mobilisé le secteur privé pour la phase 2 du programme conjoint Gouvernement-ONU. Bilan phase pilote 2021-2023 : près de 2 millions de jeunes connectés, 1 043 emplois directs, 2 500 indirects et 6 663 jeunes formés. Objectifs phase 2 : 5 000 jeunes vers l'emploi et l'auto-emploi, 500 entrepreneurs innovants, 2 500 capacités renforcées et 30 000 jeunes sensibilisés à la santé reproductive. C'est un appel au co-investissement pour la jeunesse que le Ministre de la Jeunesse et de l'Education Civique a lancé à Douala. Le 10 septembre 2026, dans les services du Gouverneur du Littoral Samuel Ivaha Diboua, Mounouna Foutsou a présidé une rencontre stratégique avec chefs d'entreprises et organisations citoyennes autour de la phase 2 du Programme conjoint Gouvernement-ONU Youth Connekt Cameroon. Lancé en décembre 2019 sous le haut patronage du Président Paul Biya, le programme a bouclé sa phase pilote 2021-2023 sur un bilan jugé significatif par le MINJEC. Place désormais à la phase 2, effective depuis 2025, avec l'entrée de l'UNICEF et du Centre des Nations Unies pour les Droits de l'Homme et la Démocratie en Afrique centrale. L'ambition est de changer d'échelle. Pour y parvenir, Mounouna Foutsou a invité les entreprises à rejoindre l'écosystème et à publier offres d'emploi, de financement et de stages via les plateformes Youth Connekt et institutionnelles. « Il y a de la place pour tout le monde », a-t-il lancé. Une dynamique que le Ministre veut voir se consolider pour faire du jeune Camerounais un véritable acteur du développement inclusif et durable. Cet article Youth Connekt Cameroon : le privé appelé à amplifier la phase 2 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Financement SND30 : le Cameroun séduit les investisseurs à Londres
data.description: © DR Les 9 et 10 septembre 2026, le Cameroun a mené à Marlborough House à Londres un Market Sounding avec le Commonwealth Enterprise and Investment Council. Objectif : mobiliser de nouveaux capitaux pour la SND30. Avec 3,5% de croissance en 2025, une dette à 43,7% du PIB et 88 000 milliards FCFA d'investissements à trouver, Yaoundé veut passer du potentiel aux projets bancables. C'est une offensive de charme financier que le Cameroun a menée à Londres. Les 9 et 10 septembre 2026, une délégation conduite par le Ministre des Finances, Louis Paul Motaze, a participé à un Road Show organisé avec le Commonwealth Enterprise and Investment Council (CWEIC) à Marlborough House. Le message est clair : il ne s'agit plus simplement d'emprunter davantage, mais de mieux financer le développement, à travers des capitaux à coûts soutenables, des garanties et des financements mixtes basés sur le partage des risques. Devant investisseurs et institutions financières, le Cameroun a fait valoir ses fondamentaux. Selon les chiffres présentés, l'économie affiche 3,5% de croissance en 2025 pour la 3e année consécutive, avec un PIB nominal de 34 474 milliards FCFA dont près de 98% tiré du non-pétrolier. La dette publique ressort à 43,7% du PIB à fin 2025, bien en deçà du plafond CEMAC de 70%. L'enjeu est colossal : près de 88 000 à 89 000 milliards FCFA d'investissements nécessaires pour la SND30, dont 45% attendus des partenaires au développement et du secteur privé. Énergie avec plus de 12 GW de potentiel hydroélectrique, infrastructures, mines, agro-industrie, numérique et eau urbaine ont été présentés comme secteurs prioritaires. Le Cameroun mise aussi sur la finance durable, avec son cadre adopté en 2024, les obligations vertes et sociales, et la finance carbone adossée au Bassin du Congo. Pour 2026, 406 milliards FCFA de dépenses budgétaires favorables au climat sont annoncés. L'ambition : transformer le potentiel en projets bancables capables d'attirer du long terme. Cet article Financement SND30 : le Cameroun séduit les investisseurs à Londres est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Investissement et commerce extérieur : les chiffres clés de 2025 au Cameroun
data.description: © DR Selon le rapport de l'Institut national de la statistique (INS) publié en septembre 2026, l'investissement progresse de 1,9% en 2025 après 4,3% en 2024 pour une contribution de 0,4 point au PIB. Le privé rebondit à +6,6% après +0,4%, tandis que le public recule de -0,2% après +18,8%. Les exportations reprennent à +1,0% après -5,1%, mais les importations s'accélèrent à +5,1% après -2,9%. Le solde extérieur pèse à -0,8 point contre -0,2 point en 2024. D'après le rapport sur la situation économique 2025 publié par l'Institut national de la statistique, l'investissement confirme son ralentissement. Il augmente de 1,9% en 2025, après une hausse de 4,3% en 2024, relève l'INS. Cette évolution résulte d'une progression de la formation brute de capital fixe de 5,1% et d'une contribution négative de la variation des stocks. L'investissement contribue pour 0,4 point à la croissance du PIB. Le privé à +6,6% prend le relais d'un public en repli Le rapport de l'INS met en évidence une rupture entre les deux composantes. L'investissement privé retrouve du dynamisme avec une croissance de 6,6% après 0,4% en 2024. Cette progression, souligne l'Institut, s'explique notamment par la poursuite des investissements dans les secteurs agro-industriel, manufacturier, minier et des infrastructures productives. Plusieurs projets structurants dans les secteurs agricole, industriel et minier ont été engagés ou mis en service en 2025, renforçant progressivement les capacités de production nationales. À l'inverse, l'investissement public affiche une légère contraction de 0,2%, après une forte croissance de 18,8% en 2024, d'après l'INS. Exportations : légère reprise de 1,0% S'agissant du commerce extérieur, l'INS note une légère reprise des exportations en volume de 1,0% en 2025, après le repli de 5,1% enregistré en 2024. Cette amélioration résulte principalement de la reprise des exportations de services (+21,0% après -21,8%), tandis que les exportations de biens reculent de 3,8%. Les exportations contribuent positivement à la croissance du PIB à hauteur de 0,2 point, après une contribution négative de 0,9 point en 2024. Importations à +5,1% : le solde se dégrade à -0,8 point L'Institut pointe une accélération des importations en volume à 5,1% en 2025, après une baisse de 2,9% en 2024. Cette hausse est portée à la fois par les importations de biens (2,3%) et surtout par les importations de services (24,2%). Les importations contribuent négativement à la croissance du PIB à hauteur de 1,0 point, contre une contribution positive de 0,6 point en 2024. En définitive, conclut l'INS, le solde des échanges extérieurs de biens et services a davantage pesé sur la croissance économique en 2025. Sa contribution à la croissance du PIB est négative et estimée à -0,8 point, contre -0,2 point en 2024. Cet article Investissement et commerce extérieur : les chiffres clés de 2025 au Cameroun est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun/ Fraude pétrolière : le Minee enchaîne les coups, plus de 5 000 litres saisis en une semaine
data.description: © DR La Brigade nationale de lutte contre la fraude des produits pétroliers est sur tous les fronts. En moins d'une semaine, deux opérations d'envergure ont permis de saisir 5 275 litres de carburant illicite. La première opération s’est déroulée à Yaoundé et ses environs entre le 09 et le 11 septembre 2026. Sur instructions du ministre Gaston Eloundou Essomba, elle a duré 72 heures de traque intensive. Accompagnés des Forces de maintien de l'ordre, les brigadiers ont passé au peigne fin les sites de contrebande identifiés sur renseignement à Olembé, Nkometou, Boumnyebel, Mfou, Sombo, Monti. L'opération visait aussi les stations-service pour faire respecter la circulaire du 21 mars 2023 qui interdit la vente de carburant dans des récipients non conformes de plus de 100 litres. Au terme de l’opération, le bilan est de 1 075 litres de carburants saisis. La seconde opération est un coup de filet de la Brigade sur l’axe Sangmélima dans la région du Sud. Elle s’est déroulée du 12 au 13 septembre 2026. Sur renseignement, les équipes ont effectué une nouvelle intervention. Cette fois, les brigadiers ont suivi et intercepté un camion transportant du gasoil dissimulé dans un compartiment. Le bilan est plus lourd. 4 200 litres de gasoil saisis. Pour un bilan cumulé de 5 275 litres de carburants frauduleux saisis en une semaine. Le ministre des Transports rappelle que le secteur aval est strictement encadré par le décret n°2000/935/PM du 13 novembre 2000. D’après ce cadre règlementaire, le stockage, le transport, la distribution des produits pétroliers hors circuit réglementaire constituent la fraude. Ainsi, à la suite de ces saisies, le ministère affiche l’objectif de ‘’poursuivre sans relâche ces opérations sur l'ensemble du triangle national" pour assainir les circuits d'approvisionnement. Cet article Cameroun/ Fraude pétrolière : le Minee enchaîne les coups, plus de 5 000 litres saisis en une semaine est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.translatedDescription: © DR La Brigade nationale de lutte contre la fraude des produits pétroliers est sur tous les fronts. En moins d'une semaine, deux opérations d'envergure ont permis de saisir 5 275 litres de carburant illicite. La première opération s’est déroulée à Yaoundé et ses environs entre le 09 et le 11 septembre 2026. Sur instructions du ministre Gaston Eloundou Essomba, elle a duré 72 heures de traque intensive. Accompagnés des Forces de maintien de l'ordre, les brigadiers ont passé au peigne fin les sites de contrebande identifiés sur renseignement à Olembé, Nkometou, Boumnyebel, Mfou, Sombo, Monti. L'opération visait aussi les stations-service pour faire respecter la circulaire du 21 mars 2023 qui interdit la vente de carburant dans des récipients non conformes de plus de 100 litres. Au terme de l’opération, le bilan est de 1 075 litres de carburants saisis. La seconde opération est un coup de filet de la Brigade sur l’axe Sangmélima dans la région du Sud. Elle s’est déroulée du 12 au 13 septembre 2026. Sur renseignement, les équipes ont effectué une nouvelle intervention. Cette fois, les brigadiers ont suivi et intercepté un camion transportant du gasoil dissimulé dans un compartiment. Le bilan est plus lourd. 4 200 litres de gasoil saisis. Pour un bilan cumulé de 5 275 litres de carburants frauduleux saisis en une semaine. Le ministre des Transports rappelle que le secteur aval est strictement encadré par le décret n°2000/935/PM du 13 novembre 2000. D’après ce cadre règlementaire, le stockage, le transport, la distribution des produits pétroliers hors circuit réglementaire constituent la fraude. Ainsi, à la suite de ces saisies, le ministère affiche l’objectif de ‘’poursuivre sans relâche ces opérations sur l'ensemble du triangle national" pour assainir les circuits d'approvisionnement. data.title: Cameroun : la croissance maintenue à 3,5% en 2025
data.description: © DR Selon le rapport sur la situation économique 2025 publié en septembre 2026 par l'Institut national de la statistique (INS), le PIB national affiche une croissance stable à 3,5% dans un contexte mondial à 3,5%. Le tertiaire reste le moteur à +4,3% et le secondaire se redresse à +2,6%, compensant le ralentissement du primaire à +1,8%. Une croissance portée par la consommation à +4,6% mais freinée par un commerce extérieur à -0,8 point. D'après le rapport annuel de l'Institut national de la statistique (INS) publié en septembre 2026, l'économie nationale a fait preuve de résilience en 2025 en maintenant son rythme de croissance à 3,5%. Une performance réalisée dans un contexte international marqué par une croissance mondiale demeurée stable à 3,5%, en raison du ralentissement des échanges internationaux, du repli de l'inflation et de la baisse des cours des produits énergétiques. Offre : le tertiaire tire, le primaire cale L'analyse de l'INS par secteur d'offre révèle des dynamiques contrastées. Le secteur primaire ralentit sensiblement à 1,8% après 3,6% en 2024, en lien avec la décélération de l'agriculture à 1,1%. Une contre-performance atténuée par la poursuite du dynamisme de l'élevage (3,8%) et de la pêche (4,8%). Le secteur secondaire améliore sa performance avec une croissance de 2,6% après 1,7% en 2024. Selon l'Institut, ce redressement est porté par les industries agroalimentaires (3,6%), les autres industries manufacturières (4,4%) et les BTP (4,3%), mais demeure freiné par la contraction des industries extractives. Le secteur tertiaire reste le principal moteur de la croissance avec une progression de 4,3%, soutenue notamment par les services d'information et communication (10,3%) et les activités financières (9,2%). Demande : la consommation compense le déficit extérieur Du côté de la demande, l'INS souligne que la consommation finale demeure le principal soutien de l'activité avec une hausse de 4,6%, portée par sa composante privée (4,9%). L'investissement progresse de 1,9%, sous l'effet du regain de l'investissement privé, tandis que l'investissement public ralentit. Les exportations de biens et services augmentent légèrement de 1,0%, mais les importations progressent davantage (5,1%). Ainsi, le solde des échanges extérieurs contribue négativement de 0,8 point à la croissance du PIB, contre -0,2 point en 2024. En perspectives pour 2026, l'INS estime que l'économie devrait continuer de bénéficier de la dynamique des investissements productifs engagés dans les secteurs agricole, industriel et minier, dans un contexte de poursuite de la désinflation mondiale et de persistance des tensions géopolitiques. Cet article Cameroun : la croissance maintenue à 3,5% en 2025 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
